CIRCUIT 16 / QUICK GUIDE

A little pattern.
A world of motion.

Press Play to start the six-part studio. All parts share one clock; their individual lengths and speeds create the movement.

Shape a sequence

Move a slider to set a note. Tap a lit square to silence that step. Tap a note name to audition it once audio is on. Shift-click a step to tie it to the previous note.

Hear the drums

Each percussion row has a sound selector: choose any MIDI key in the current kit. The list shows the key number, note, and instrument name. Keys without samples are marked. Click ▶ beside a row to hear it, even with playback stopped. Assignments belong to the pattern and are saved with your project. Turning on a drum step also auditions it while stopped. Use LEVEL for the whole drum machine and the row sliders for individual sounds. The line under the grid explains any mute, solo, zero level, or empty pattern. Percussion stays clear when the melodic filter closes; delay and reverb still apply.

Enter pitches with MIDI

Connect your keyboard, click Connect MIDI, allow access, and choose its input. Select a melodic track or bass, turn Step Entry on, and click a step number or note name. Play one key to fill that step. Auto-advance moves to the next step and wraps at the track length. Use key velocity also records how hard you play; otherwise existing dynamics stay. MIDI follows the current scale; choose Chromatic for every note. Turn Step Entry off when finished. MIDI needs a browser with Web MIDI support and may require opening the HTTPS site in its own tab.

Go beyond pitch

Use Velocity, Gate, Chance, and Repeat to change step dynamics, duration, probability, and ratchets. Notes follow the selected key and scale. Choose a chord or octave in each module.

Make patterns move

Change Length, Rate, or direction independently. A seven-step sequence will cycle against a sixteen-step one. Motion slowly sweeps the filter; Evolve gently varies note velocity.

Copy a part

In Part Copy / Paste, choose a melodic sequence, BASS, All drums, or one drum row and press Copy Part. Choose the destination pattern A–H and destination part, then Paste Part. Sequences include all 16 steps, dynamics, ties, and timing settings; drum rows copy their rhythm and follow the destination drum machine’s timing. The destination instrument stays unless Include sound is checked. Melody and bass can exchange sequences while keeping their own sound engines. A drum row with sound copies its key and level within the destination kit. The copied part stays available for more pastes until replaced or the page is reloaded. Every paste can be undone. Copy All / Paste All above still copies the entire pattern.

Build an arrangement

Patterns A–H store notes, instruments, and sequence settings. A pattern selected during playback starts at the next bar. Copy and paste patterns to develop them. Enable Chain to follow a sequence such as A:4 B:4 C:8; numbers are bars. The chain loops.

Keep your music

Edits autosave in this browser. Save downloads a portable project; Load opens it. Preset changes can be undone. Rec captures live playback and knob movements as WAV—press it again to finish. WAV Export renders the current pattern or chain with an eight-second effects tail.

Stay in control

M mutes; S solos. The mixer and effects are shared across patterns. Space plays/stops; Ctrl/⌘ Z undoes. Keep the page open while recording. Full screen is best for a large touch display.
